title: Sunday Pot Roast with Carrots and Potatoes
description: Beef chuck seared and braised low and slow in the oven with red wine, onions, and thyme, then finished with carrots and potatoes that cook in the same pot. The braising liquid becomes a simple gravy.
notes: Cut: chuck roast is the right choice here; lean roasts such as round turn dry. Doneness: beef is safe at 145°F with a 3-minute rest, but chuck only becomes tender at about 195 to 205°F, so cook until a fork twists easily in the thickest part rather than by the clock. Without wine: replace it with 1 more cup of broth plus 1 tablespoon red wine vinegar. Gluten-free: the gravy is thickened with cornstarch; check the broth and tomato paste labels. Make-ahead: pot roast reheats very well. Cool, refrigerate in its liquid, lift off the hardened fat the next day, and rewarm covered at 300°F for 30 to 40 minutes. Storage: refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 4 days, or freeze the meat in its gravy for up to 3 months (the potatoes do not freeze well).

ingredients.name: boneless beef chuck roast, tied if loose
neutral oil, such as avocado or canola
medium yellow onions, cut into thick wedges
carrots, peeled and cut into 2-inch pieces
Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks
cornstarch, stirred into 1 tablespoon cold water

instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the lower third. Pat the roast very dry and season it on all sides with 2 1/2 teaspoons of the salt and all of the pepper.

Heat the oil in a 5- to 6-quart Dutch oven over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Sear the roast, turning with tongs every 4 to 5 minutes, until every side is deep brown, 12 to 15 minutes total. Move it to a plate.

Lower the heat to medium and add the onions. Cook, scraping up the browned bits, until they soften and pick up color, 5 to 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook until the paste turns brick red, about 1 minute. Pour in the wine and simmer until reduced by about half, 2 to 3 minutes.

Add the broth, thyme, and bay leaves and bring to a simmer. Return the roast and any juices to the pot; the liquid should reach about halfway up the meat. Cover, transfer to the oven, and braise for 2 hours, turning the roast over once after the first hour.

Arrange the carrots and potatoes around the roast, pushing them into the liquid, and sprinkle them with the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt. Cover and braise until a fork twists easily in the center of the roast (about 195 to 205°F) and the vegetables are tender when pierced, 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes more.
Lift the roast and vegetables onto a platter, cover loosely with foil, and rest for 15 minutes. Discard the thyme stems and bay leaves and skim the fat from the surface of the liquid.
Bring the liquid to a simmer over medium heat. Whisk in the cornstarch mixture and simmer, whisking, until the gravy lightly coats a spoon, 1 to 2 minutes. Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed.
Slice the roast thickly across the grain, or pull it into large chunks, and serve with the vegetables and gravy.

title: Oven Pulled Pork with Tangy Barbecue Sauce
description: Pork shoulder coated in a smoky brown sugar rub, roasted low until it shreds with a fork, and tossed with a quick ketchup-and-vinegar barbecue sauce built on the pan juices. Slow cooker directions are in the notes.
notes: For deeper seasoning, rub the pork and refrigerate it, covered, for up to 24 hours before cooking. Doneness: pork is safe at 145°F, but shoulder will not shred until it reaches about 195 to 205°F; if a fork meets resistance, keep cooking and check every 20 minutes. Slow cooker: place the rubbed pork in the cooker with the water and vinegar and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours or on high for 5 to 6 hours, until fork-tender; for crisp edges, spread the shredded pork on a sheet pan and broil for 3 to 4 minutes. Serving: pile onto buns with slaw and pickles, or serve over rice or baked potatoes. Storage: refrigerate within 2 hours, with some of the juices, for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months; reheat covered with a splash of water until steaming hot (165°F). The sauce contains mustard. The ingredients are not gluten-containing as written, but check the labels on the ketchup, mustard, and spices if cooking gluten-free.

ingredients.name: boneless pork shoulder (Boston butt), cut into 2 equal pieces

instructions: Heat the oven to 300°F with a rack in the lower third. Stir the rub ingredients together in a small bowl and set aside 1 tablespoon for the sauce. Pat the pork dry and press the remaining rub over every surface.
Set the pork fat side up in a 5- to 6-quart Dutch oven. Pour the water and 1/4 cup vinegar around the meat, not over it, so the rub stays in place. Cover and roast for 3 hours.

Uncover the pot, spoon some of the juices over the pork, and roast uncovered until the top is dark and crusted and a fork twists easily in the thickest part, 30 to 45 minutes more. A thermometer should read about 195 to 205°F.
Move the pork to a large bowl or rimmed sheet pan and rest for 20 minutes. Pour the pan juices into a measuring cup and spoon off the fat that rises to the top.

While the pork rests, combine the ketchup, 1/3 cup vinegar, 1/4 cup brown sugar, mustard, reserved tablespoon of rub, and 1/2 cup of the skimmed pan juices in a small saucepan. Simmer over medium-low heat, stirring often, until glossy and thick enough to coat a spoon, 8 to 10 minutes.

Shred the pork with two forks, discarding any large pieces of fat. Toss it with about half of the sauce and a few spoonfuls of the remaining pan juices until moist. Taste, add a pinch of salt if needed, and serve with the rest of the sauce at the table.

title: Sheet-Pan al Pastor-Style Pork Tacos with Pineapple
description: Thin slices of pork shoulder marinated in guajillo chile, pineapple juice, and garlic, roasted hot and broiled with fresh pineapple until the edges char. A home-oven take on the flavors of tacos al pastor.
notes: Marinating time is not included: plan on at least 2 hours and up to 12 hours in the refrigerator. Use canned or bottled pineapple juice in the marinade; raw pineapple juice contains an enzyme that turns pork mushy over a long soak. Slicing is easier if the pork is firmed in the freezer for 30 minutes first. Traditional al pastor is cooked on a vertical spit and often includes achiote paste; if you have it, blend in 1 tablespoon. Skillet option: cook the drained pork in a very hot cast-iron skillet in 3 batches, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Food safety: discard any marinade left in the bowl, and cook the pork to at least 145°F (thin slices will go well past this by the time they char). Gluten-free: use tortillas made only from corn and pure ground chile. Storage: refrigerate cooked pork within 2 hours for up to 4 days; reheat in a hot skillet.

ingredients.name: dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
boneless pork shoulder, sliced 1/4 inch thick across the grain

instructions: Cover the guajillo chiles with very hot water in a small bowl and soak until soft and pliable, about 15 minutes. Drain, keeping a few tablespoons of the soaking water.

Blend the softened chiles with the pineapple juice, vinegar, garlic, oil, salt, chipotle powder, oregano, and cumin until completely smooth, about 1 minute, adding 1 to 2 tablespoons of soaking water only if the blender stalls. The marinade should be a thick, pourable paste.
Toss the sliced pork with the marinade in a bowl until every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours and up to 12 hours.

Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack about 6 inches below the broiler. Line a rimmed sheet pan with foil. Lift the pork from the bowl, letting the excess marinade drip off, and spread it on the pan in a single layer. Scatter the pineapple in the gaps.

Roast until the pork is cooked through and most of the liquid on the pan has evaporated, 12 to 15 minutes. Switch the oven to broil and cook, watching closely, until the edges of the pork and pineapple are charred in spots, 3 to 5 minutes.
Rest the pork for 5 minutes, then chop it and the pineapple into bite-size pieces on a cutting board and toss them with any juices left on the pan.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet over medium-high heat until soft and lightly toasted, 20 to 30 seconds per side, stacking them in a clean towel as you go.
Fill each tortilla with pork and pineapple and top with onion and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing.

title: Lamb Kofta with Garlic-Mint Yogurt Sauce
description: Ground lamb mixed with grated onion, parsley, mint, cumin, and a little cinnamon, shaped into small logs and browned in a skillet. Served with a cool, garlicky yogurt sauce. No breadcrumbs needed.
notes: Twelve kofta serve 4 as a main with rice, flatbread, or a tomato-cucumber salad. Squeezing the grated onion dry matters: extra moisture makes the kofta fall apart. The 20-minute chill (not included in the times) also helps them hold their shape. Food safety: ground lamb must reach 160°F in the center. Grill or broiler: thread onto flat metal skewers if you like and cook over medium-high heat or 4 inches under the broiler for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once. Substitutions: ground beef, or half beef and half lamb, works with the same seasoning and the same 160°F target. Make-ahead: shape the kofta up to 24 hours ahead and refrigerate, covered; the sauce keeps for 3 days. Storage: refrigerate cooked kofta within 2 hours for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 2 months.

ingredients.name: medium yellow onion, grated on the large holes of a box grater and squeezed dry

instructions: Wrap the grated onion in a clean towel or a few paper towels and squeeze firmly over the sink until no more liquid drips out.

Combine the onion, lamb, 2 cloves garlic, parsley, 2 tablespoons mint, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, 1 1/4 teaspoons salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Knead with your hands until the mixture looks uniform and feels slightly tacky, about 1 minute.
With damp hands, divide the mixture into 12 portions and shape each into a log about 3 inches long and 1 inch thick. Set them on a plate and refrigerate for 20 minutes to firm up.
Meanwhile, stir the yogurt, remaining clove of garlic, lemon juice, 1 tablespoon mint, and 1/4 teaspoon salt together in a small bowl. Refrigerate until serving.

Heat the oil in a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over medium heat until it shimmers. Add the kofta, leaving space between them (work in two batches if needed), and cook, turning every 2 to 3 minutes, until well browned on all sides and 160°F in the center, 10 to 12 minutes.
Rest the kofta on a plate for 3 minutes, then serve warm with the yogurt sauce.

title: Red Wine Beef Stew with Mushrooms and Pearl Onions
description: A bourguignon-style stew: beef chuck browned in bacon fat and braised in red wine and broth until spoon-tender, then finished with butter-browned mushrooms and pearl onions.
notes: Wine: use a dry red you would drink, such as Pinot Noir or Cotes du Rhone; avoid bottles labeled cooking wine, which are salted. Buy a whole chuck roast and cut it yourself; packaged stew meat is often a mix of cuts that cook unevenly. Doneness: beef is safe at 145°F, but chuck needs the full braise to turn tender, so cook until a piece crushes easily against the side of the pot. Make-ahead: the stew tastes better the next day. Refrigerate, lift off the fat, and reheat gently over medium-low heat, adding a splash of broth if it has thickened. Serve over mashed potatoes, buttered noodles, or with crusty bread. Storage: refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months.

ingredients.name: boneless beef chuck, trimmed and cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
medium carrots, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
frozen pearl onions, thawed and patted dry

instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the lower third. Cook the bacon in a 5- to 6-quart Dutch oven over medium heat, stirring now and then, until crisp and the fat has rendered, 6 to 8 minutes. Scoop the bacon onto a plate, leaving the fat in the pot.

Pat the beef dry and season it with 2 teaspoons of the salt and all of the pepper. Raise the heat to medium-high and brown the beef in 3 batches, turning the pieces until deeply browned on at least two sides, 5 to 6 minutes per batch. Move each batch to the plate with the bacon.

Lower the heat to medium and add the chopped onion and carrots. Cook, scraping the bottom of the pot, until the onion softens, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook until the paste darkens, about 1 minute. Sprinkle in the flour and stir until no dry spots remain, about 1 minute.

Pour in the wine, scrape up everything stuck to the pot, and simmer for 3 minutes. Add the broth, thyme, bay leaves, beef, bacon, and any juices from the plate. The liquid should come nearly to the top of the meat. Bring to a simmer.
Cover, transfer to the oven, and braise until a piece of beef crushes easily against the side of the pot, 2 hours to 2 hours 30 minutes.

About 20 minutes before the stew is done, melt the butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms in an even layer and cook, stirring only occasionally, until browned, 6 to 8 minutes. Add the pearl onions and the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt and cook until golden in spots, 4 to 5 minutes.

Set the pot on the stovetop over medium-low heat and stir in the mushrooms and pearl onions. Simmer uncovered until the sauce coats the back of a spoon, about 10 minutes. Discard the thyme stems and bay leaves and skim any fat from the surface.
Taste and add up to 1/2 teaspoon more salt if needed. Let the stew stand for 10 minutes before ladling into bowls.

title: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Dijon-Thyme Pan Sauce
description: Thick bone-in pork chops seared until golden and kept juicy by pulling them at the right temperature, with a quick pan sauce of shallot, white wine, Dijon mustard, and a little butter.
notes: Chops about 1 inch thick give you time to build a crust before the center overcooks; thinner chops cook in roughly half the time. For better seasoning, salt the chops and refrigerate them uncovered for 1 to 24 hours, then let them stand at room temperature for 20 minutes before cooking. Food safety: USDA guidance for whole cuts of pork is 145°F followed by a 3-minute rest; the center will still be slightly pink and juicy at that temperature. Without wine: use 1/2 cup more broth and add 2 teaspoons white wine vinegar or lemon juice with the mustard. Boneless chops of the same thickness cook 1 to 2 minutes faster. Gluten-free: check the broth and mustard labels. The sauce contains mustard. Storage: refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 3 days; reheat gently in a covered skillet with a splash of broth.

ingredients.name: bone-in pork rib chops, about 1 inch thick (about 10 oz each)
neutral oil, such as avocado or canola
cold unsalted butter, cut into 4 pieces

instructions: Pat the chops very dry and season both sides and the edges with the salt and pepper. Let them stand at room temperature for 20 minutes while you prepare the sauce ingredients.

Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers and just begins to smoke. Lay the chops in the pan, leaving space between them (sear in two batches if they crowd), and cook without moving until the undersides are deep golden brown, 4 to 5 minutes.

Flip the chops, lower the heat to medium, and cook until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part, away from the bone, reads 140°F, 4 to 6 minutes more. Use tongs to stand each chop on its fatty edge for about 30 seconds to render and brown it.
Move the chops to a plate and rest for 5 minutes; the temperature should climb to at least 145°F. If it does not, return the chops to the pan for a minute per side.

Pour off all but about 1 tablespoon of fat from the skillet and set it over medium heat. Add the shallot and cook, stirring, until softened, 1 to 2 minutes. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.

Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits. Simmer until reduced by about half, about 2 minutes. Whisk in the broth and mustard and simmer until the sauce is reduced by half again and looks lightly syrupy, 3 to 4 minutes.

Take the skillet off the heat and whisk in the butter one piece at a time until the sauce is glossy. Stir in the thyme and any juices from the resting plate, taste, and add a pinch of salt if needed. Spoon the sauce over the chops and serve.

title: Shepherd's Pie with Lamb and Buttery Mashed Potatoes
description: Ground lamb simmered with onion, carrots, peas, and thyme in a savory gravy, covered with buttery mashed potatoes and baked until the top is golden and the edges bubble.
notes: Shepherd's pie is traditionally made with lamb; use the same amount of ground beef and the dish becomes cottage pie. Food safety: ground lamb and beef must reach 160°F, which the filling does by the time it has browned and simmered. Worcestershire sauce contains anchovies (fish). If you do not have an oven-safe skillet, transfer the filling to a 2 1/2-quart baking dish before topping. Make-ahead: assemble, cool, cover, and refrigerate for up to 2 days; bake from cold at 400°F for 35 to 40 minutes, until the center is hot (165°F). Storage: refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours for up to 4 days, or freeze, tightly wrapped, for up to 2 months. Reheat until steaming hot throughout.

ingredients.name: russet or Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks
medium carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4-inch dice

instructions: Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water by 1 inch, and add 1 teaspoon of the topping salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then lower to a steady simmer and cook until a knife slides through a chunk with no resistance, 15 to 18 minutes.

Drain the potatoes, return them to the hot pot, and let the steam cook off for 1 minute. Mash with the butter, warm milk, and remaining 3/4 teaspoon topping salt until smooth and fluffy. Cover and set aside.

Heat the oven to 400°F. Set a 12-inch oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat and add the lamb. Cook, breaking it into small pieces, until no pink remains and the meat starts to brown, 6 to 8 minutes. Spoon off all but about 1 tablespoon of fat.

Lower the heat to medium and add the onion, carrots, 1 teaspoon salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring often, until the vegetables soften, 6 to 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, and thyme and cook until the paste darkens, about 1 minute.

Sprinkle the flour over the filling and stir for 1 minute. Pour in the broth and Worcestershire sauce and simmer, stirring, until the gravy is thick enough to hold a line when you drag a spoon across the pan, 5 to 6 minutes. Stir in the peas and take the skillet off the heat.
Spoon the potatoes over the filling, starting around the edge to seal it, then spread to cover. Rough up the surface with a fork so it browns well.
Set the skillet on a rimmed sheet pan and bake until the filling bubbles at the edges and the potato peaks are golden, 20 to 25 minutes. For a darker top, broil for 1 to 2 minutes, watching closely.
Let the pie rest for 10 minutes so the gravy settles before scooping out portions.

title: Sheet-Pan Italian Sausage with Peppers and Potatoes
description: Italian sausages roasted on one pan with bell peppers, red onion, and golden potatoes, then finished with a splash of red wine vinegar and parsley. A full dinner with about 15 minutes of prep.
notes: Use fresh (raw) sausage links, not precooked. Most Italian sausage is free of gluten and dairy, but some brands add fillers or cheese, so read the label if that matters for your table. Do not prick the sausages; the casings hold in the juices. Food safety: fresh pork sausage must reach 160°F in the center (165°F if you substitute chicken or turkey sausage). A crowded pan steams instead of browning, so use the largest sheet pan you have or split everything between two pans. Serving: eat as is, or pile into rolls. Storage: refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 4 days; reheat on a sheet pan at 400°F for about 10 minutes.

ingredients.name: small Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 3/4-inch pieces
bell peppers (a mix of red, yellow, and orange), cut into 3/4-inch strips
large red onion, cut into 1/2-inch wedges
fresh sweet or hot Italian pork sausage links (gluten-free; about 6 links)

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the center. In a large bowl, toss the potatoes, peppers, and onion with the oil, oregano, salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes until evenly coated.
Spread the vegetables on a rimmed sheet pan in a single layer, turning the potatoes cut side down. Roast for 15 minutes, until the potatoes are starting to brown underneath.
Stir the vegetables, then nestle the sausages and garlic cloves among them so the sausages sit directly on the pan.
Roast, turning the sausages once halfway through, until they are browned and 160°F in the center, the potatoes are tender, and the peppers are charred at the edges, 20 to 25 minutes more.
Drizzle the vinegar over the vegetables, toss them with the pan juices, and scatter the parsley on top. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Caramelized Lemongrass Pork with Fish Sauce and Lime
description: Thin slices of pork shoulder marinated in fish sauce, brown sugar, lemongrass, and garlic, then seared in a hot skillet until sticky and browned at the edges. Served over rice with lime-dressed cucumber. Contains fish sauce.
notes: This recipe is seasoned with fish sauce, which is made from anchovies and supplies nearly all of the salt in the dish; there is no substitute that keeps the same flavor. Marinating time is not included: 30 minutes is the minimum and up to 8 hours in the refrigerator is better. Lemongrass: use only the pale, tender lower part of the stalk and mince it very finely; 3 tablespoons of refrigerated lemongrass paste can stand in. The sugar in the marinade browns fast, so lower the heat if the pan starts to smoke heavily. Food safety: pork should reach at least 145°F (thin slices go well past that), and the leftover marinade must come to a full boil in the pan before serving. Fish sauce is usually gluten-free, but a few brands contain wheat protein, so check the label if needed. Storage: refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 3 days.

ingredients.name: lemongrass stalks, tough outer layers removed, tender lower 4 inches finely minced
boneless pork shoulder, sliced 1/4 inch thick into bite-size pieces
fresh lime juice, plus lime wedges for the table

instructions: Stir the fish sauce, brown sugar, lemongrass, garlic, shallot, pepper, and 1 tablespoon of the oil together in a mixing bowl until the sugar dissolves. Add the pork and toss until every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes and up to 8 hours.
Toss the cucumber with the lime juice and salt in a small bowl and set aside while you cook the pork.

Heat 1/2 tablespoon of the remaining oil in a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until it just begins to smoke. Lift half of the pork from the marinade, letting the excess drip back into the bowl, and spread it in a single layer. Cook without stirring until deeply browned underneath, 2 to 3 minutes, then flip and cook until the second side is browned and the pork is cooked through, 1 to 2 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Repeat with the remaining 1/2 tablespoon oil and the rest of the pork, lowering the heat to medium if the browned bits on the pan look close to burning.

Return all of the pork to the skillet over medium heat. Add the marinade left in the bowl along with 2 tablespoons water and cook, stirring, until the liquid comes to a full boil and reduces to a sticky glaze that clings to the meat, 1 to 2 minutes.
Spoon the pork over the rice and add the cucumber alongside. Top with the scallions, cilantro, and chile, and serve with lime wedges.

title: Cast-Iron Strip Steaks with Chimichurri
description: Thick strip steaks salted ahead, seared hard in a cast-iron skillet, rested, and sliced under a sharp parsley, garlic, and red wine vinegar chimichurri. Includes pull temperatures for every level of doneness.
notes: Doneness after resting: rare 125°F, medium-rare 130 to 135°F, medium 140 to 145°F, medium-well 150 to 155°F, well-done 160°F and above. Take the steaks off the heat about 5°F below your target, since the temperature keeps rising as they rest. USDA guidance for whole cuts of beef is a minimum of 145°F followed by a 3-minute rest. Salting: the 30- to 45-minute rest after salting is not included in the times; for an even better crust, salt the steaks and refrigerate them uncovered on a rack for up to 24 hours. Ribeye or sirloin of the same thickness cooks the same way. Two 12-ounce steaks, sliced, serve 4 with sides; for one steak per person, cook in two batches or two skillets. Searing produces smoke, so turn on the vent fan. Chimichurri keeps, covered and refrigerated, for 3 days; bring it to room temperature before serving. Refrigerate leftover steak within 2 hours for up to 3 days.

ingredients.name: boneless New York strip steaks, 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 inches thick (about 12 oz each)
high-heat neutral oil, such as avocado
packed fresh flat-leaf parsley leaves and tender stems, finely chopped

instructions: Pat the steaks dry and season all over with 1 1/2 teaspoons salt. Let them stand at room temperature for 30 to 45 minutes; the surface will look moist at first and then dry again.

For the chimichurri, stir the garlic, shallot, vinegar, 3/4 teaspoon salt, and red pepper flakes together in a bowl and let stand for 5 minutes to mellow the garlic. Stir in the parsley, oregano, and olive oil. Set aside at room temperature.

Heat a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over high heat until very hot, 3 to 4 minutes. Pat the steaks dry again and season with the pepper. Add the neutral oil to the skillet; it should shimmer and just start to smoke.
Lay the steaks in the skillet, away from you, and sear without moving until a dark brown crust forms, about 3 minutes. Flip and sear the second side for 3 minutes.

Lower the heat to medium and keep cooking, flipping every minute and holding each steak on its fatty edge with tongs for 30 to 60 seconds, until an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 5°F below your target: 125 to 130°F for medium-rare or 135 to 140°F for medium, 2 to 5 minutes more.
Move the steaks to a cutting board and rest for 8 to 10 minutes. The temperature will rise about 5°F as they rest.
Slice the steaks across the grain about 1/2 inch thick. Stir the chimichurri, spoon some over the meat, and serve the rest alongside.
